## Historical audit: S0010

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is visible; citations below refer to that file and the supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal and build — student `model_request`, JSONL line 13, chars [0,181568) | The requested goal was a photograph-matched indoor reconstruction with separate meshes and a matching camera. The student’s inventory *interpreted* the scene as a windowed cafeteria. Its first program constructed multiple architecture, furniture, pendant, plant and accessory assets, using named child parts, colored materials, a camera and area lights. These names and inventory are not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Validation and revision — line 13, chars [0,181568) | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and took 37.54 seconds. The student then described the foreground pendant and palm as outside the framing, booth/chair placement errors, gray exterior and insufficient furniture contrast. This is the student’s diagnosis, not a visual finding independently verified here. |
| Executed changes — line 13, chars [0,181568) | The revised program moved the pendant, palm, booths, chairs and right wall; darkened several finishes; changed lighting and exterior emission; and retained the same camera settings. It retained composite parts such as chair seat, back, stem and base, and applied chair rotations. Code establishes intended hierarchy and placement, not physical connection, correct pose or visual match. Colors, roughness and emission are specified; no image texture is used in the visible code. |
| Final validation — line 13, chars [0,181568); student `codex_session`, line 14, chars [0,3854); student `model_response`, line 15, chars [0,351) | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, a saved render and blend file, and 35.88 seconds. The final session was supplied the reference and both render paths, had no tool calls, and returned `DONE`. The images themselves are not visible to this audit, and the final response gives no detailed comparison. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** The visible record contains system instructions and runner feedback, but no identifiable teacher diagnosis, proposed update or teacher-directed execution. Thus teacher receipt or adoption is not established; the student’s first-render comparison and revision are the visible autonomous exploration. No conclusion about unseen chunks follows.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Both executions formally succeeded; the last successful build was to be submitted automatically under the stated procedure. This is technical build/render success, not verified reconstruction success or an independently established partial-correctness score. No empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption is visible. Whether multiple objects actually appear in frame, their materials resemble the reference, parts meet correctly, object orientations match, or camera, lighting and rendering defects were resolved remains unknown without the images or geometric inspection.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a rendered first build can support an explicit discrepancy list and a targeted second execution, while successful rendering alone cannot validate fidelity. Task-specific hypotheses—especially whether the shifted palm and pendant, brighter exterior and unchanged camera improved this cafeteria view—remain unverified.
